responsibilities: Design and own the core data models that everything else depends on, making them clean, trusted and easy to build on.
Work inside the product and engineering codebase to ensure data is captured and structured correctly from the start, before it ever reaches the warehouse.
Build and maintain the pipelines that connect our systems, so data flows through the business correctly and reliably.
Make the data platform genuinely self-serve, so product, growth, commercial and ops teams (and our agents) can answer their own questions without coming to you.
Treat agents as first-class consumers of the data layer, structuring data so they can do analytical work accurately and at scale.
Partner with the team on the metrics that matter, from acquisition and activation through to matching quality and commercial performance.
Turn ambiguous business questions into the right data model, the right metric and a clear answer.
Set the standards for data quality, definitions and instrumentation across Dex.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Design and own the core data models that everything else depends on, making them clean, trusted and easy to build on.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities stress "clean, trusted" models, data flowing "correctly and reliably" and "standards for data quality"; the only speed phrase ("We move quickly") describes the interview process.
evidence.domain_risk: Our matching, our product decisions, our growth, our commercial bets all depend on understanding what's actually happening across the business
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: A talent marketplace where errors affect "product decisions" and "commercial bets" but carry no regulatory or financial-reporting exposure.
evidence.data_team_maturity: As the first dedicated data hire, you'll set the standards and build the function out behind you as Dex grows.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Explicitly "the first dedicated data hire" building the function, so the data team is early stage.
evidence.jd_authorship: Work inside the product and engineering codebase to ensure data is captured and structured correctly from the start, before it ever reaches the warehouse.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities are specific to Dex's setup (modelling at source, agents as consumers, matching quality metrics), so a reader can picture the day-to-day.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: the data platform that the whole company (and our agents) builds on top of
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The primary audience is the company's data consumers (teams and agents) served via "the data platform" and self-serve, rather than one business function.
evidence.autonomy_level: Design and own the core data models
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Founding role that will "own the data foundation of Dex end to end" and "set the standards", which is strategic ownership.
evidence.ai_role: Treat agents as first-class consumers of the data layer, structuring data so they can do analytical work accurately and at scale.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds and structures data that AI agents consume, making AI downstream of their output.
evidence.testing_framing: Set the standards for data quality, definitions and instrumentation across Dex.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality standards are an owned responsibility, though no testing tools are named.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: so data flows through the business correctly and reliably
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Reliability and trust matter but are framed as enabling speed ("force multiplier") rather than preventing compliance or trust failures.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: building on what's already driving the business rather than starting from a blank page
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: A founding data role that defines the foundation, but explicitly builds on existing systems rather than a blank page.
evidence.loss_aversion: Get it right and every person and every agent at Dex gets faster and  sharper. — quality framed as upside for speed rather than risk reduction.
